run.note: A scratch --data-root, never ~/.ai-raccoon. Driven over stdio MCP by a small client (scratchpad/mcpcli.py) after a one-shot pipe failed to capture JSON-RPC frames.

derived.note: Counted from the tree at run time, then CONFIRMED against the live server's tools/list and prompts/list.

items.expected-result: Release build and pack succeed; the global tool force-updates and `ai-raccoon --version` matches derived.version
items.evidence: 9 packages including ai-raccoon.1.14.0.nupkg and all 7 RID packages | Tool 'ai-raccoon' was successfully updated from version '1.13.0' to version '1.14.0'. | 1.14.0+56d35d837e551422dd276521a095c0b18ef3b8d3
items.observed-result: Pack produced every RID package; the tool reports the derived version with the HEAD sha.
items.acceptation-reason: Version and +sha both match `git rev-parse HEAD` exactly.

items.expected-result: `serve --port 0` binds and reports its port; `serve --restart` stops the incumbent and serves in its place
items.evidence: Now listening on: http://127.0.0.1:60857 | http://127.0.0.1:60857/mcp | ServerRestart[651] the server on port 60857 (pid 70117) stopped and the port is free | first server's own log: Application is shutting down...
items.observed-result: Port 0 bound and printed both URL and /mcp entry; --restart named the incumbent by pid, confirmed the port free and bound in its place.
items.acceptation-reason: The incumbent's shutdown is confirmed from its own log, not inferred from the restarting process.

items.expected-result: A write returns stored:true with a content-derived hash and path
items.observed-result: Both a substantive and a one-character write stored, each with a distinct content-derived hash and path.
items.acceptation-reason: stored:true is corroborated by memory_get returning the value below.

items.expected-result: A natural-language query returns the written entry with a ranking and a snippet
items.evidence: results[0] = {hash 011c14bd..., ranking 1, snippet "The retention reaper purges a promotion discard only once its entry is…"}, correlationId 01a004f6dfb0...
items.observed-result: Top hit is the written entry; a correlationId is issued, so the search_quality row this release now reaps is being written.
items.acceptation-reason: Hit identity checked by hash, not by snippet text.

items.expected-result: memory_get on the search hit's hash returns the exact stored value
items.evidence: {"hash":"011c14bd...6f76","value":"The retention reaper purges a promotion discard only once its entry is gone.","context":"project:checklist"}
items.observed-result: Byte-exact round trip of the written content.
items.acceptation-reason: Compared against the string written earlier in the same session.

items.expected-result: An ingested file is chunked, and a `file.md#section` query returns that file's chunks carrying sourceFile
items.evidence: ingest {"indexed":1} | anchored query returned chunkIndex 3 and 1 of totalChunks 5, both sourceFile .../0055-a-discard-is-load-bearing-while-its-entry-lives.md
items.observed-result: One file ingested into 5 chunks; the anchored query returned chunks of that exact file with source identity attached.
items.acceptation-reason: First attempt returned `path-outside-scope` — CORRECT: the ingest allowlist is empty by default. Re-run after `ingest scope add`, which is the documented precondition, not a workaround.

items.expected-result: A write matching a noise policy is refused with stored:false and a named reason
items.evidence: "[IMPORTANT: Background process..." -> {"stored":false,"reason":"rejected by noise policy 'HermesBackgroundProcessLog'"} | "received signal 15" -> same
items.observed-result: Both shapes the policy names are refused, with the truthful outcome ADR-0032 requires: empty hash, stored:false, named policy.
items.acceptation-reason: An earlier probe using a `<background_process_notification>` block WAS stored. Read HermesProcessNoisePolicy before reporting it: the policy names three exact shapes and that is not one of them, so storing it is correct. The probe was wrong, not the product.

items.expected-result: A query containing log output is annotated; a query that IS machine output is refused
items.evidence: warn tier: "info: ...BankMaintenanceHostedService[510] Bank WAL checkpoint complete" -> results plus warning "This query contains what looks like log or stack-trace output..." | refuse tier: "[IMPORTANT: Background process bg_1 completed normally]\nCommand: npm run dev" -> invalid-params: "This looks like tool output rather than a question..."
items.observed-result: Both tiers fire with their ADR-0040 guidance text.
items.acceptation-reason: A first refuse-tier probe carried the prefix but neither co-marker and came back clean. QueryGuardPolicy requires prefix AND (`completed normally` | `Command:`) — deliberate, and its own comment says so: the read path demands two signals where the write path needs one. Clean was correct; the probe was under-specified.

items.expected-result: memory_watch_add registers a watch and memory_watch_status reports it
items.observed-result: Watch registered and reported in Scanning state.
items.acceptation-reason: Before `watch enable checklist true`, add returned the typed refusal `watching-disabled` and status stayed empty — correct for a disabled feature, and the refusal is typed rather than a crash.

items.expected-result: memory_promotion_list and memory_stats answer for a fresh project
items.evidence: promotion_list -> {"rows":[]} | stats -> {"entries":3,"pending":3,"contexts":["project:checklist"]} | every response envelope carries meta.waitingPromotionsCount 0
items.observed-result: Empty queue on a fresh bank; stats count the writes made in this session and name the one context.
items.acceptation-reason: entries=3 matches the three writes that were not noise-rejected.

items.expected-result: initialize + tools/list + prompts/list return derived.mcp-tool-count tools and derived.mcp-prompt-count prompts
items.observed-result: Live surface matches the counts derived from the tree, and serverInfo reports the release version.
items.acceptation-reason: The counts were derived from the tree FIRST and then confirmed against the server, so neither number was copied from the other.

items.expected-result: The maintenance pass logs its registered event ids, including WP7's new 522-524
items.evidence: BankMaintenanceHostedService[510] Bank WAL checkpoint complete (observed at both startup and shutdown of both servers) | IdleWatchdog[610] idle watchdog armed (04:00:00) | ServerRestart[650]/[651]
items.observed-result: 510, 610, 650 and 651 observed. Event ids 522-524 (the retention reapers this release adds) were NOT observed: their pass runs on the maintenance cadence and there was nothing to purge on a bank minutes old.
items.acceptation-reason: Four event ids confirmed live, but the three THIS RELEASE introduces were not exercised. Their integration test (RetentionReaperTests) covers the purge; what is unverified here is that the hosted service reaches them on a real cadence. Needs a run with the retention window set short against a bank with aged rows.

items.expected-result: An unrecognised verb is passed through to the proxy without polluting the JSON-RPC channel or failing the process
items.evidence: `ai-raccoon --data-root <scratch> notaverb` -> rc 6, stderr "Unrecognized command or argument 'notaverb'." followed by the proxy dialling POST http://127.0.0.1:7721/mcp
items.observed-result: It does fall through — the proxy starts and dials the backend — but it first prints 'Unrecognized command or argument' and the process exits with code 6.
items.acceptation-reason: REPEAT of the 1.13.0 failure, unchanged. Falling through is only half the contract: the stray line and the non-zero exit are both observable by a client that passed an unknown argument, and rc 6 makes a wrapper treat a working proxy as a failed launch.
